---
mode: agent
description: Generate, curate and commit the visual assets a site shows — imagery, personas and cinematic motion — from a configured backend, under the ui-visual-assets guardrails.
---
You are running the **visualize** workflow (`knowledge/rigor-protocol.md`), governed absolutely by **`knowledge/ui-visual-assets.md`** (VA1–VA22), over `ui-design-craft.md` (DX4/DX5/DX16/DX19), `ui-interaction-design.md` (U11, U13–U17) and `ai-commercial-models.md` (AC2–AC3). Convene **UX & Accessibility** (lead — register, alt text, contrast over imagery; **hard veto**), **Product Strategist** (does this serve the job or is it decoration), **Domain Researcher** (establish the backend contract and licence terms, never recall them), **The Simplifier** (**soft veto** — does this asset earn its weight; the honest answer is often no), **AI Systems Engineer** (**hard veto** — non-determinism in a committed artifact, and the spend), **Privacy & Data Governance** (**hard veto** — likeness, personal data, egress), and **SRE** (the performance budget, which generated assets blow more often than anything else).

**The one rule to internalise: generate what the interface SHOWS, never the interface itself** (VA5). Ask an image model for "a better version of this page" and you get malformed text and invented controls — an image that looks finished and encodes nothing anyone can build. Generate the photograph inside the card; hand-author the card.

**Ground first** in `DESIGN.md` (tokens + any existing `assets:` manifest), the direction brief if one exists, the surface that will render the asset (**open it — never describe it from memory**, E15), and the VA-* defect classes. Then run `python3 docs/ai-forward-pack/scripts/visual-assets-setup.py --check` to establish which backend is actually reachable. **If none is confirmed, stop and say so** rather than describing images you cannot produce.

**Establish the entitlement before designing around it (VA19).** *"I have a Google subscription"* does **not** mean an agent can generate: a consumer Google AI Pro/Ultra plan grants the Gemini app, Flow and Whisk and grants **no API access at all**; the API is a separate billing relationship (an AI Studio key on a Cloud project with active billing), and **image and video generation are not on the free tier**. Ask of any backend: which account holds it, does it expose an **API** rather than only a web app, and is the capability on the tier being paid for.

**State the mode: board · asset · persona · motion.** Default to **board** when unclear — a concrete visual reference is cheap and prevents the expensive mistake of generating a dozen finished assets in the wrong register. **If the request is "beautify" or similarly open, narrow it first**: it means either *make the visual design better* (that is `/ui-design`, and imagery will not fix hierarchy, spacing or type), *add imagery the page displays* (this skill), or *make the direction concrete* (board mode). Name which before generating anything.

**Interdict the rush: generate nothing yet.** Generation is the cheapest step to start and the most expensive to redo at scale — forty images in the wrong register cost forty times one image in the wrong register.

**OPEN — the register, in words.** Atmosphere, palette temperature, material, era, light; the **anti-goals**; the **slot list** (each asset with its rendered dimensions, aspect ratio, and whether text sits over it); and a **stated budget** before the first call (VA10 — batch exploration is where budgets die). Choose presets from the **product-appropriate subset**, not the whole catalogue (VA3). **Mood never structure** (VA6) and **never instead of a real named reference** (VA7 — a generated image is evidence of nothing).

**INTERROGATE.** Per slot: what job does this image do that type and space could not (if there is no good answer, the Simplifier already won)? What sits over it, at what contrast? What is the largest rendered dimension, and therefore the resolution actually needed? Does it need consistency with another asset, and therefore a character or style reference? Is the layout still sound if it fails to load?

**EVIDENCE — generate into scratch.** Candidates go to **`docs/assets/<surface>/_scratch/`** (git-ignored): exploration is not a commit. Record the **verbatim prompt, backend, model and preset** as you go, never afterwards. Poll async jobs to a terminal state and treat failure and content-refusal as ordinary outcomes, not crashes (VA2). Prefer **one better prompt over ten samples**.

**DISCONFIRM — cull hard; this is where the value is.** Reject against the **imagery tells** (VA8: teal-and-orange grading, impossible bokeh, glossy plastic skin, symmetrical hero compositions, stock-mimicry, subtly wrong geometry) and against the brief's **anti-goals**. Ask the Simplifier which slots are better served by **nothing at all**. Check **licence and likeness** at time of use (VA9, VA11) — no recognisable real person, trademark or brand. Measure **contrast on the composite** where text sits over imagery (VA18).

**CONVERGE — commit the survivors.** **Download immediately and commit** (VA4 — provider results expire; a committed provider URL is a broken image with a delay timer). **Optimize** to the budget: modern format, sized to the largest rendered dimension, explicit `width`/`height` against layout shift, responsive sources, lazy-load below the fold (VA14, U17). Write the **manifest entry** in `DESIGN.md` (VA12: id, file, purpose, backend, model, preset, verbatim prompt, date, cost, alt text, disclosure, licence-checked) and the **alt text now** (VA13 — the prompt is not alt text). **Motion** additionally carries a poster frame, a `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback, a text alternative, and a motion-inventory entry (VA17). Re-run `ui-craft-gate.py` over the rendering surface (`broken-image`, `text-occlusion`, `low-contrast`) and confirm the budget holds. Delete unchosen `_scratch/` contents and **state the spend**. End with the status table (Completed | Remaining | Best next action).

**Last action — discoverability (V10):** assets are **data**; the graph node is the surface's hub `.md` (or `docs/assets/<surface>/README.md`) with V2 frontmatter and typed links to the design language and the surface it serves. Sync via `python3 docs/ai-forward-pack/scripts/docs-graph.py derive` (V18). A changed direction board or replaced hero is **material** — flag `DESIGN.md`, the spec's Part C and the mockup `review-suggested` (V16). Capture the register decision **and the rejected candidates** as a decision note in `docs/notes/` (V17) — the rejected direction is what people re-litigate. Register any new failure as a class (CI1).

**Running this in Copilot (single agent — make the dialog visible).** Enact the round-table inline: label each peer's contribution, then run the adversary round with a severity **[Blocker|Major|Minor|Nit]** per finding and an explicit **PASS/BLOCK** plus veto-clears-when for the hard-veto roles. The culling dialog is the deliverable.

**Audit (last action):** `python3 docs/ai-forward-pack/scripts/audit-log.py append --shortname "visualize-<surface>" --session "<id>" --skill visualize --kind skill --prompt "<verbatim>" --summary "<slots filled, spend>" --artifact docs/assets/<surface>/…` (AL5); add a change-log entry when the run settles the visual direction (CL1).
